en: The Apadāna of the Elder Sīhāsanabījiya Jagatidāyaka Chapter, Number 3 The Apadāna of the Elder Sīhāsanabījiya: I gave a lion-throne to the Buddha, the Teacher, who was seated upon it; By that merit, I have attained the state of an Arhat. I am now free from birth, old age, and death; Having abandoned all suffering, I have reached the end of existence. I have attained the cool state, the blissful Nibbāna. I have crossed over the ocean of saṃsāra. I have attained the supreme, unsurpassed security. I have realized the goal for which I went forth. I have become one who has done what was to be done. I have laid down the burden and am liberated. I have lived the holy life and have exhausted the taints. I have no further existence. I am a sage, a conqueror, and a victor. I am a field of merit for the world. I am a refuge for those who seek shelter. I am a lamp for those in darkness. I am a boat for those crossing the flood. I am a bridge for those seeking the further shore. I am a physician for the sick. I am a mother for the motherless. I am a father for the fatherless. I am a kinsman for those without kin. Thus indeed did the Venerable Elder Sīhāsanabījiya speak these verses.
The legend of the Elder Sīhāsanabījiya is the third.
